profiles.name: Faraz Martin Talab
profiles.description:
Faraz Martin Talab was one of the eleven defendants in the San Diego County District Attorney's prosecution of anti-fascist counter-protesters who attended the January 9, 2021 "Patriot March" pro-Trump rally on the Pacific Beach boardwalk. He was sentenced on June 28, 2024 by San Diego Superior Court Judge Daniel B. Goldstein to a term in the 180-day to 2-year range in the Pacific Beach 8 sentencing.

On January 9, 2021 — three days after the Capitol riot in Washington, D.C. — pro-Trump organizers held a rally they called the "Patriot March" along the boardwalk in the Pacific Beach neighborhood of San Diego, California. A group of anti-fascist counter-protesters appeared and confrontations broke out, including the use of pepper spray, the throwing of objects, and several physical assaults. The San Diego County District Attorney brought conspiracy-to-riot and related charges against eleven counter-protesters under what would become, when sentenced in 2024, the first major state-level "antifa" conspiracy prosecution in the United States. Nine of the eleven pleaded guilty; two were convicted at jury trial in May 2024. On June 28, 2024, San Diego Superior Court Judge Daniel B. Goldstein sentenced the eight named defendants to terms ranging from 180 days in county jail to two years of state prison.
profiles.finding: San Diego indictment and court briefs corroborate defendant. Aggregator links an LA public-records request as potential original source; no recognizable verified portrait accepted.

profiles.name: Christopher Kent Podlesnik
profiles.description: Christopher Kent Podlesnik, age 52, of Laramie WY, left threatening voicemails for Senators Cynthia Lummis, John Barrasso, Rep. Matt Gaetz, and a state senator on January 28, 2021, calling them traitors and threatening to shoot them. Pleaded guilty to four counts; 18 months federal prison.
profiles.finding: WakeUpWyo named case report located. University honor-roll surname results not identity evidence; no portrait verified.

profiles.name: Rickey Johnson
profiles.description: Rickey Johnson, age 47, of New York, sent threatening messages on January 30, 2021 to U.S. Senator Joe Manchin and Fox News hosts Laura Ingraham and Greg Gutfeld. Convicted at trial; 72 months federal prison.
profiles.finding: DOJ complaint/appellate case and WDTV confirm Manhattan threats defendant. Louisiana Innocence Project exoneree and unrelated booking images rejected.

profiles.name: John Subleski
profiles.description: John Subleski, age 32, of Louisville KY, a member of the United Pharaohs Guard Boogaloo militia, was charged with using social media to incite a riot in downtown Louisville on January 6, 2021 contemporaneous with the U.S. Capitol riot, posting Time to storm LMPD and similar messages. Pleaded guilty; sentenced to time served (5 months) and 3 years probation.
profiles.finding: WAVE3 sentencing report and GWU-hosted defense memorandum are strong case/photo leads; image inspection remains.

profiles.name: Cornelius C. Allen
profiles.description: Cornelius C. Allen, 45, of Tampa, FL was charged with burglary of an unoccupied structure, felony rioting, and one misdemeanor count of petty theft following his involvement in a May 31, 2020 BLM protest. He was observed removing approximately $50.00 worth of merchandise from a local Walgreens and attempting to leave. Pleaded no contest to theft and burglary; rioting charge dismissed. Sentenced to 1 day confinement (effective January 12, 2021).
profiles.finding: Exact-name query yielded no usable identity-specific portrait; unrelated county record results not accepted.

profiles.name: Thomas Alexander Starks
profiles.description: Thomas Alexander Starks, age 30, of Lisbon ND, used an axe to smash the entrance window of a Republican U.S. Senators Fargo office in late 2020 in frustration over the lack of a Covid-19 relief vote. Pleaded guilty; sentenced to time served (~7.8 months).
profiles.finding: Case-specific Fargo axe news/repost lead located; original source/portrait inspection pending.

profiles.name: Peter James Yeager
profiles.description: Peter James Yeager, 45, USMC veteran, drove from Grand Coulee WA to Spokane on December 9, 2020 with a preconceived plan to burn down the Spokane County Democrats office in the Teamsters Building, telling people he had a bomb. Possessed staged-bomb props but no actual completed device. Found not guilty by reason of insanity in March 2024 in federal court.
profiles.finding: Govinfo case and Inlander report corroborate Grand Coulee defendant. No individual portrait verified.

profiles.name: Rowan McManigal
profiles.description: Rowan McManigal, age 19, was sentenced April 15, 2022 to 3 years probation under a guilty plea for possession of a hoax destructive device (a self-igniting Molotov cocktail) at a protest outside a Portland ICE facility.
profiles.finding: Exact-name search yielded case-list material but no verified portrait; historical text matches unrelated.

profiles.name: Javon Hardy
profiles.description: Javon Hardy, 24, set fire to a 32-by-8-foot mobile office at the Rochester Public Safety Building during the May 30, 2020 BLM protest, captured on Facebook Live yelling Let that bitch burn. Charged December 15, 2020. Pleaded guilty; 12 months federal prison + $14,504 restitution.
profiles.finding: DOJ Rochester sentencing source corroborates person. Tennessee assault defendant, obituary and Pride Arts namesakes unlinked; rejected.

profiles.name: Aline Espinosa-Villegas
profiles.description:
Aline "Ángel" Espinosa-Villegas is a trans woman federally prosecuted for arson committed during the George Floyd Uprising protests in Little Rock, Arkansas in 2020. She pleaded guilty to federal arson and is serving her sentence at FMC Carswell. She is expected to face ICE detention upon release due to her immigration status.

Aline A. Espinosa-Villegas, 24, of Little Rock AR, Jeffrey et al. co-defendant for the August 2020 Molotov attacks on Little Rock police vehicles. Pleaded guilty; 18 months federal prison + $34,356.31 restitution.

Angel Espinosa-Villegas is a Chilean-born trans butch lesbian organizer who came to the United States at age seven and built her life in Chicago. She was one of the four Little Rock, Arkansas defendants — alongside Mujera Benjamin Lunga’ho, Renea Goddard, and Cody Nowlin — federally prosecuted for the torching of Little Rock police vehicles during the protests following the police murder of George Floyd. In September 2022 she pleaded guilty to possession of a Molotov cocktail and was sentenced to 18 months in federal prison, which she served at the Federal Medical Center at Carswell in Fort Worth, Texas.

On April 1, 2025, at the end of her federal sentence, she was taken into ICE custody for deportation to Chile. After several months in immigration detention she was deported and reunited with family in Chile, separated from her partner, family, and community in the United States.
profiles.finding: It's Going Down support reporting located; needs named portrait/source inspection. No verified image accepted.

profiles.name: Emily Nowlin
profiles.description: Emily Nowlin, 27, of Little Rock AR, was indicted December 14, 2020 in the Jeffrey et al. case for August 2020 Molotov-cocktail attacks on police vehicles at the Little Rock PD 12th Street Substation and Arkansas State Police Headquarters. Pleaded guilty; 18 months federal prison + $35,956.31 restitution.
profiles.finding: Little Rock case material/New Tolerance lead found. Indianapolis State Farm agent rejected as unrelated. No verified portrait.

profiles.name: Michael Patschak
profiles.description: Michael Patschak is a Maryland activist who participated in the Black Lives Matter protests of 2020. On December 12, 2020, at Black Lives Matter Plaza on 16th Street NW in Washington, D.C., Patschak intervened when police were arresting fellow demonstrators, attempting a de-arrest. During the confrontation he took a police body-worn camera and later returned to the scene, where he was identified and arrested after punching an officer. He was convicted at trial in November 2022 on two counts of assaulting a police officer and one count of robbery. He was sentenced to a suspended term with 15 days to serve, a $200 fine, and one year of probation.
profiles.finding: DC courts brief and Patch case report corroborate person. Running-site2015 image possible lead but no independent identity link yet.

profiles.name: Samantha Frances Brooks
profiles.description: Samantha Frances Brooks is a Bellingham, Washington activist who placed a shunting device on BNSF railroad tracks near Bellingham with Ellen Reiche on November 28, 2020, in solidarity with the Wetsuweten hereditary chiefs opposing pipeline construction across British Columbia. A shunt makes a stretch of track read as occupied, which halts trains; the two were arrested at the scene and charged in December 2020 under 18 U.S.C. § 1992, the federal statute covering terrorist attacks and other violence against railroad carriers. Brooks pleaded guilty in July 2021 and was sentenced in October 2021 to six months in federal prison, four months of home confinement, three years of supervised release and 200 hours of community service — a lighter sentence than Reiche received. The Bureau of Prisons, where she was register number 19550-509, records her as out of custody on May 20, 2022.
profiles.finding: DOJ complaint corroborates name. Co-defendant Ellen Reiche photo must not be substituted; extremist reposts not sufficient verification.

profiles.name: Rene Christopher Bracamonte
profiles.description: Rene Christopher Bracamonte, age 34, threatened the life of former Vice President Mike Pence at the Westin La Paloma Hotel in Tucson AZ on August 11, 2020. He pulled a handgun and waved it in the air after departing the resort. Pleaded guilty; 6 months federal prison.
profiles.finding: Exact-name query did not yield verified portrait. LinkedIn directory partial matches insufficient.

profiles.name: Khalif Miller
profiles.description: Khalif Miller is a North Philadelphia father and small business owner indicted in October 2020 by Trump U.S. Attorney General William Barrs Department of Justice on federal charges arising from the May–June 2020 protests in Philadelphia following the police murder of George Floyd. He was one of five Philadelphians charged in a coordinated indictment alongside Ant Smith. He was held on pretrial detention for two years before pleading and was sentenced to five years in federal prison. Because he was on probation at the time of his indictment, he was given an additional 1 to 10 year Pennsylvania state sentence for probation violation, to which he is now serving after completing his federal time. The Uprising Support project documented his case as one of the most aggressive examples of federal prosecution of 2020 uprising defendants.
profiles.finding: Truthout case article directly inspected: lead image is general George Floyd vigil, not named portrait, rejected. Inquirer/support-project portrait leads remain.

profiles.name: Haley Rainwater
profiles.description: Haley Rainwater was one of six people arrested October 9, 2020 in Collierville TN after spray-painting and throwing adhesive and feathers on a Confederate statue. Charges dropped prior to trial.
profiles.finding: WVLT/Collierville Herald case identifies defendant. Music profiles not independently linked. Arrest collage needs positional identity/crop verification.

profiles.name: Dylan Davis
profiles.description: Dylan Davis was arrested in connection with Lancaster’s September 2020 racial-justice protest and spent September 14–17 in jail before release to house arrest. A November 2022 bench trial resulted in six convictions, including riot and conspiracy. He was sentenced to probation in February 2023.
profiles.finding: WGAL named memoir interview and Lancaster DA case source located. Texas/SC bookings, jockey and unrelated Dylan Davis records rejected. Interview image inspection pending.

profiles.name: Barry Jones III
profiles.description: Barry Jones III was detained after Lancaster’s September 2020 protest following Ricardo Muñoz’s death. He left jail on September 17 for house arrest. In July 2022 he was convicted of failure to disperse and received a time-served-to-twelve-month sentence. The twelve-month maximum is not a finding that he served that entire period.
profiles.finding: WGAL bail coverage identifies Barry Jones30/III; no individually verified portrait obtained.
